answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a meaningful bond in a shared vault before it may trade. A newcomer starts with no reputation and earns trust only through small, verifiable jobs, like a falcon proving itself on short flights before it is trusted to hunt at the zenith. If the agent cheats, the bond is slashed and its history is burned, so spawning a hundred fake identities costs a hundred bonds while honest work compounds into one valuable reputation.
